Kitchsmart 10 LED, USB, Dimmable Light Wand for PC or Laptop Powered by Multiple Sources with Applications Both Indoors and Outdoors for Notebook Travelers Camping Hiking Reading Writing I love this light, absolutely love it. I purchased a laptop without backlit keys thinking I wouldn't be using it all that often but a disability has led me to require the touch-pad on the laptop as using a mouse on my desktop had become a near impossibility. I had come across another flexible USB lighting system that was less than half the height of this light and also lacked the on/off function as well as the dimmer capability which I find extremely useful.
When plugged into my rear most USB port this light reaches just above the top of the screen on my 15.6" laptop and with the light dimmed somewhat it doesn't glare even where it's just an inch or so from the screen itself but sheds enough light that I can see the entire keyboard easily.
The neck is strong enough to hold its position while standing there as well as once it's unplugged and put on the table when the laptop is not in use. It does wiggle a bit at the USB port but I think all USB ports seem to have a little wiggle room built into them.
Control couldn't be easier though controls would have, to me, been more convenient. You quickly press/tap the end of the USB light bar very, very lightly to turn or off the light. Dimming the light requires holding the end as the light dims or releasing it and holding it again as the light brightens. Personally I think separate switches would be more convenient but the single switch works well enough.
I love this light. It's absolutely perfect for my needs and puts so much more light on the keyboard than the smaller light I previously used (shown in one of the photos I'll attach) plus the fact that I can turn it on and off as well as dim or brighten the light just adds to the usefulness of the light. This also works great with a USB power pack.
I received this light in exchange for my review.

text_fidelity_a:
WixGear Sport Wireless Earbuds, Bluetooth 5.0 Wireless Over Ear Sport Headphones with Touch Control, and Charging Case Stereo Deep Bass Sound,30H Playtime Sweat-Proof Bluetooth Earphones with Mic For my uses, these are great. They were very well packaged and secure for shipping. The box is very nice and sturdy, lined with foam. I need to hear the environment around me. This has been an issue with previous earbuds. Commercials between videos or songs can get so loud! That is the deal-breaker for me, as it's a safety issue. These do not get too loud, even on the loudest setting, so I am able to remain safe. I don't have an issue hearing the sounds coming from the buds, but I'm not in high-traffic outdoor areas regularly either. My ear canals are unusually small for an adult. I was afraid these may be too-big, but they are snug. Any bigger and it may have been an issue. I used the smaller of the plastic tips. Over the ear designs are the only ones that have ever worked for me. I did look at some other models in the past, but I found them a bit more expensive than I felt justified to spend unknowing how well they may work for me. However, knowing how well these work, I find them to be a really great value and would have purchased them before if I had known how well they worked. It was only by chance they were up for review and I had been seeking a replacement on my old pair that I've been using for the past few years.

The Bluetooth is nice. I have a simple cell phone. It only took asking my phone to connect to work. It was the easiest that I have ever had with connecting anything Bluetooth to my phone. I liked this as I'm not the most savvy at using Bluetooth electronics. If I can do it, anyone can.

I'm not great at using the buttons as they are really sensors on the flat-side of the body on the earbuds. I'm getting used to it but they are touch sensitive and there is a correct spot and amount of pressure that works best. I'm still getting a feel for it and there is a slight delay, so it's very easy to double-tap. The included booklet has been helpful to learn to use these straight out of the package.

Sometimes I get down on the floor at the gym to use the foam rollers and stretches, other times I'm using them in the car to take calls. I've tried them at work as well. Every scenario has worked well for me. I really do wish I've had these before. Sometimes while getting my breaks at work, I would want to listen to things from my phone, but didn't want to risk disturbing my co-workers with some of the news and hobby related videos I enjoy. I asked a few co-workers if they could hear my earbud noise, they could not.

The case is very easy to use as well and fits easily into my pockets. I'm a lady, so my pockets are not always very generously sized. It charges very quickly, and I've not found myself running out of charge. I cannot speak on the long-term durability for this as they are new. If/when I experience any issues with the charge, I will be sure to post an update.

In summary, these would be better for users that need to hear their surroundings for safety. For those that want extreme high volume, they may not be as happy. They stay on my ears securely and the case works very well. I'm pleasantly surprised how well I like these and hope that they are durable since they are working so well for me.

Thanks for reading my review. I hope you found it helpful.
text_fidelity_b: WixGear Sport Wireless Earbuds, Bluetooth 5.0 Wireless Over Ear Sport Headphones with Touch Control, and Charging Case Stereo Deep Bass Sound,30H Playtime Sweat-Proof Bluetooth Earphones with Mic

Dragon Touch Classic 15 Digital Picture Frame, 15.6” FHD Touch Screen WiFi Digital Photo Frame Instant Share Photos and Videos via App, Email, Cloud, Wall Mountable, Portrait and Landscape Where do I start? This is the Second one of these that I ordered; sent the first one back to Amazon. I should have left it at that; but, it was the wife's birthday and we had a ton of pictures of the Grand Kids and she wanted to see them without using her phone.
This was a great idea but it simply is not worth the hassle. I downloaded the OurPhoto App to my Samsung phone and followed the instructions to "Bind" the phone to the frame and also to "Bind" the PC's email to the Frame; Both said it Bound to the Frame. The Frame showed the Bound App and the email. Great? No! The phone showed ALL of the pictures I sent were successfully transferred. Where? I do not know; they Did Not show on the Fame. If you find my pictures, let me know, because they are not transferred to the Frame!
I then decided to connect the supplied USB cable to the phone and to the Frame. NO CAN DO!
The USB cable supplied is the antique USB standard to Mini USB, not, sports fans, the USB "C" that has been the standard for several years. So I had to connect the Samsung to the PC using the proper USB to USB "C" cable and transfer each picture INDIVDUALLY to the PC, Then I had to connect the Frame to the PC using the supplied USB/Mini USB and Again transfer each picture to the Frame, one by one.
I found out when that was completed, the picture would not fit the Frame's display without modifications.
text_fidelity_b: Dragon Touch Classic 15 Digital Picture Frame, 15.6” FHD Touch Screen WiFi Digital Photo Frame Instant Share Photos and Videos via App, Email, Cloud, Wall Mountable, Portrait and Landscape

HP ENVY 6055 Wireless All-in-One Printer, Mobile Print, Scan & Copy, HP Instant Ink ready, Works with Alexa (5SE16A) I really like this HP ENVY 6055 WIRELESS ALL-IN-ONE PRINTER (5SE16A). Finally I’m able to print anything and everything from my Samsung Galaxy S10 cell phone! To set it up with an Android phone, you need two apps from Google Play: HPSmart, and HP Print Service Plugin.

SETUP. Once you have HPSmart, you turn on the printer, open the app, and follow the prompts. The app finds the printer, helps you connect it to your home network, and takes you through the process of loading paper, installing two ink cartridges, and aligning the copier. From time to time, a prompt will tell you to press a lighted or flashing button on the printer in order to proceed.

The setup process isn’t difficult, but you should start it when you have maybe 20-30 minutes to devote to it. There are enough steps that you don’t want to get interrupted in the middle.

HPSMART APP. Something that I really love about the printer, is that I can use my phone to make it scan a document and send the document to an email address. The phone can control all of the printer functions through the HPSmart display--it just takes a tap on a virtual button. I asked the printer to print a photo from my phone’s Gallery, and it came out beautifully. The photo that I took outside my home with the phone’s camera and immediately sent to the printer also came out beautifully.

MANUAL CONTROLS. You can also control the printer manually, at least for copying. When you open the printer cover, the buttons for the number of copies and copying light up. However, this printer is easiest to control with the HPSmart app. (I need to visit the HP web site and download the full manual--the closest now is the Envy 6400 all-in-one printer manual--because the lighted buttons aren’t quite intuitive.) Other mobile devices on my home network (e.g., my iPad Air) are able to find the printer and use it like any other printer on my network.

SPEED; COPY QUALITY; INK The printer is quite fast, and the quality of the printing is excellent. The ink colors are bright and the printing is extremely crisp and clear (even with fine print). The printer uses HP 67 ink cartridges--which are definitely NOT discontinued (as another reviewer reported). My local Staples store has the ink in stock right now (July 2020).

INSTANT INK PROGRAM. If you like, you can sign up for the optional HP Instant Ink program, and the printer will automatically order ink for you. I chose the “Moderate” program, which assumes printing about 100 pages per month, for $4.99 a month (after the first 2 months’ free trial). If you don’t print that many pages, you can carry over the unused pages to a later month (up to a set number of pages). You can cancel the Instant Ink program at any time.

APPEARANCE. The printer has a sleek, low profile. It’s white, which means it will blend in with the decor of any room.
text_fidelity_b: HP ENVY 6055 Wireless All-in-One Printer, Mobile Print, Scan & Copy, HP Instant Ink ready, Works with Alexa (5SE16A)

text_fidelity_a:
BOSS Audio Systems B9351WRC Double Din, Touchscreen, Bluetooth, DVD CD MP3 USB SD AM FM Car Stereo, 6.2 Inch Digital LCD Monitor, Wireless Remote, Wireless Rear License Plate Camera. I knew, due to my disability, that I was going to need to find a professional installer to install this Boss Audio Systems B9351WRC head unit and wireless reverse camera along with two replacement door speakers I decided needed replacement (and wow, they really needed replacing). The installation took approximately three hours or so. The only problem which may not be a problem but I'm a worrier. The bracket for the wireless reverse camera somewhat, but not entirely, covers the plate expiration stickers somewhat. Other than that the head unit fit as good if not better than the stock radio fit. in the dashboard.
This radio plays AM/FM stations though there's very few decent radio stations around here. The unit also plays from USB thumb drives which plugs into a port under a panel under the volume/pause/power button. I put 600+ songs on a USB 2.0 16 GB driver and it played everything as far as I could tell. There might be a couple VBR or odd format MP3 files it may not play but I haven't gotten to them yes. Nothing's refused to play and even a couple that had imbedded album artwork actually showed up but so small it was almost impossible to see and I had no idea how to make it better. The instructions in the manual were basically "Play with things and see what happens!" more than specific directions how different functions work.
What I went with, is a 32 gig micro-SD card that had the same 600+ songs the thumb drive has. But with the micro-SD card you can close the hatch under the volume and control knob which you couldn't with the thumb drive. There's also an AUX input jack for old style MP3 players and phones.
The six inch screen is sharp and crisp. The backup camera, even with a streetlight thirty feet away had more than enough light to back out of my garage. I even backed down the street a ways in almost complete darkness and could see just fine with just the reverse lights on the car. Now as long as no cops have a problem with it I'm golden.
I tried home burned CDs and while it took a few seconds longer to recognize it played them fine. I tried store bought CDs and they played right off the bat. OH! and it plays DVD discs jut fine in case my passenger wants to watch a movie as we drive. I promise I'm no dumb enough to watch a movie while I drive.
According to the installer I can leave the micro SD card in the unit all the time. So, 600+ songs anytime I want which I can shuffle or randomly pick and play songs anytime I want. I couldn't be happier. With the stock deck I'd sometimes get to my destination just as the deck decided to recognize the CD so this deck is a godsend when I really needed a new one. Now with as many songs as I can cram into a 32 gig drive. Right now I've got 687 songs and tons of free space. I may have to start buying more music and ripping some more albums from my collection to add to my micro-SD card.
So I can play hundreds, thousands of MP3 songs on a micro-SD card. I can play CDs both homemade and store bought. I can watch DVDs on a pretty sharp (all settings can be changed in the system) the dimmer is a bit bright until it goes off completely but it's not too bad or too bright. There's a user setting EQ option as well as several other preset settings to choose from. There are options to add sound effects such as large hall, church, cavern, etc. I avoided them entirely and set my own EQ settings with the loudness off. The new speakers sound great for high end and midrange. The stock back speakers add some needed bass.
All in all? This is an affordable head unit with all the features and functions one could ask for. It comes with a remote that I'm not sure I'm even going to keep anywhere in the car. Anything you need to do can be done on the deck and no one's sitting in the back seat of a '07 Hyundai Accent, seriously. So the remote is useless but amusing.
I love this unit, the backup cam is awesome, The many ways to play music. The fit and finish, it's close to perfect.
This a little long and meandering review but I really like this radio and I'm glad I replaced the door speakers and went with a professional installer who's basically given me a lifetime warranty on his labor. I couldn't be happier.

Update 04-04-2017: It's been nearly six months since I had this head unit and backup camera installed. Radio reception is still bad, I still despise listening to radio so that's no big deal. Have kept a micro SD card loaded with hundreds of songs installed. Turn the unit on it automatically defaults to that. Everything is still working fine. Professional installation was worth the money.
text_fidelity_b: BOSS Audio Systems B9351WRC Double Din, Touchscreen, Bluetooth, DVD CD MP3 USB SD AM FM Car Stereo, 6.2 Inch Digital LCD Monitor, Wireless Remote, Wireless Rear License Plate Camera.

Bose SoundTouch 10 wireless speaker, works with Alexa - Black Bose SoundTouch 10 is an excellent system that enables you to have music, podcasts, and audiobooks available at the press of a button in any room with wifi.

The sleek black design is compatible with almost all decors, and is small enough to hide in a corner.

You can access your content via preset buttons on the top of the device or by using the remote.

Set up was easy at first and then got complicated because my PC was connected to the internet both through wifi and cable. Clearly, the cable was unnecessary, but I didn't know that. You only need one connection. I initially set up the system through my ipad air which was intuitive and only took about 10-15 minutes. The reason I had to contact customer support was I wanted to sync my iTunes library to the Bose SoundTouch. The person I spoke with was patient, knowledgeable, and solved the problem. (And, waiting for tech support only took about a minute.)

I tried the sound qulaity with both classical music and PBS news. The music sounded resonant and rich and had plenty of volume. The speech was clear and easy to understand.

NOTE: Day two. Apparently, my iTunes library is so vast (17,000 items) that it was hard to keep it synched with the Bose system. I could have synched it through Bluetooth, but that meant having to remember to Bluetooth on and off via my desktop, and I use the sound on that all the time; so, it wasn't a viable option. Another idea would be to spend $80 for a NAS drive but that didn't appeal to me, either. I will buy the 3.5mm male to male cable so I can attach my ipod directly to the speaker. It will do the trick, but is not the seamless experience I was hoping for.

I can still listen to radio stations from around the world, i Heart Radio, Pandora, and anything that's downloaded through iTunes on my ipad.

This is a great product if you use it with Bluetooth, or don't have an extensive iTunes library to sync.

I hope to have it as long as I have had my Bose radio, which is more years than I can remember.
text_fidelity_b: Bose SoundTouch 10 wireless speaker, works with Alexa - Black

text_fidelity_a:
Sangean WR-2 AM / FM-RBDS Wooden Cabinet Digital Tuning Radio (Black) First of all, my first order arrived with a small crack in the wooden cabinet and it would not turn on. I am going to give Sangean the benefit of the doubt and assume that it was shipping damage even though the box from the outside did not look like it was damaged, so I won't let this affect my rating.

But this did give me a chance to test Amazon's return policy, and I must say it was great. When I realized that I had to return the radio, I went to Amazon's website and clicked on the radio and selected "return." Then I was prompted to print a return shipping label to attach to the box when I sent it back. By the time I did that, there was an email in my in box from Amazon telling me that they were shipping a replacement to me via UPS Air. So I packed up the unit in it's original box, attached the label I had printed, and then the next day when the replacement arrived I gave the box to the UPS driver. Of course, all of this was at no additional cost to me. I was quite impressed with the whole process.

Now to the radio itself. Overall I am quite impressed with it and I am giving it four stars. For a radio of it's size, it sounds great. I have never heard a radio that small with the tight bass response that this one has. And AM radio sounds better than than it does even on my Onkyo receiver that I have in my family room.

The radio with it's wooden cabinet looks great on my nightstand and you can just tell by looking at it that it is a quality product.

The tuner's sensitivity on the FM band is good with the external wire antenna that is supplied with it. Selectivity between adjacent stations is also good. And I am getting good stereo separation when I listen with headphones. I do have one small quibble however. There is a button to switch any FM station to mono, but you have to do this individually for each station. It would have been better if you could toggle between stereo and mono for all the stations at once rather than having to do it individually for each one.

AM sensitivity is pretty good using the built in antenna. Weak stations in my area come in better than they did with my old clock radio, but I still do have some problems with the very weak stations. I could probably improve this if I bought a good external AM antenna, but I don't think I will bother to do that since I don't really listen to any of the weak stations anyway.

One reason why I got this radio was because it has a line in jack. I have connected my Directv box to it so that I can listen to the Directv music channels through the radio without having my TV set on. All I had to do was to go to Radio Shack and buy a Y adapter with two RCA plugs on one end and a 1/8" plug on the other. It works like a charm.

I also like that the display has large enough numerals that I can read it without my glasses on. However, as others have mentioned, the display defaults to the radio station frequency or the RDS display rather than to the time. To get the time display back I have to tap the display button, and it's hard to do at night in a dark room. I think it would have been better if it defaulted to the time in the first place.

Another quibble that I have is that the power button uses a bright blue light which is distracting in a dark room. They shouldn't have made it so bright. That will take some getting used to.

Also, as others have mentioned, setting the alarm is needlessly complicated as is turning it off. You need to hit three different buttons to do it. I am starting to get the hang of it, but I wish they would have just included a button which toggles the alarm on and off.

But overall I am rating this as a good four star product that could use some minor improvements. The most important thing to me is the sound quality, and that is unmatched for a radio of this size.
text_fidelity_b: Sangean WR-2 AM / FM-RBDS Wooden Cabinet Digital Tuning Radio (Black)

text_fidelity_a:
1MORE iBFree In-Ear Earphones Wireless Headphones with Bluetooth 4.2 AAC, IPX 6 Waterproof, Secure Fit, In-Line Mic for Sports Gym Running - New Model Black We blow through ear buds in our house and it seems that everyone has different ones that they like and don't like. Let's see how these measure up:

WHAT ARE THESE EAR BUDS LIKE?
These ear buds come in a nice box with a little instruction booklet. There is a little bag with three sets of gel caps in it. There are also three sets of hooks. Each of them comes in small medium and large. The hooks keep the buds in the ear but are soft so they don't hurt the ear at all.

The controls are on the right ear- the top hits about where the chin is. The connecting cord is big enough to be worn in front or back. The set comes with a cord but you have to have your own USB access to plug it into whether it be on an outlet or computer.

COMFORT
One of the most comfortable and secure earbud/headsets we have used to date- love that the hooks that help hold them in are soft so they don't hurt the ear, even after worn for a while.

PERFORMANCE
VOLUME
The headset gets the best result for us with the volume on max on the headset and halfway on the tablet that we use it with.

HIGHS/LOWS/MIDS
One of the things with this headset is that the highs are really nice and strong and so are the lows. The problem seems to be that the mids are drowned out making it feel like it is a bit out of balance. We have messed with it quite a bit and it seems to be the way it is.

SOUND PROOFING
These have excellent sound insulation capabilities. That does mean, however, that you need to be careful where you are wearing them if you need to hear what is around you or not.

BATTERY ALERT
When you first turn on the headphones, it will identify itself, tell you it is pairing and then give you an idea of how much battery life you have left- low, medium, or high.

POWER BUTTON
The power button is nice. Volume/skip functions are a challenge to get used to as compared to other Bluetooth headsets. There are sequences and timing as compared to others which seem to be simpler to use.

PAIRING
Very good pairing on all of the different devices we tested this with- several phones from Moto G3, Blu phone, Samsung Tablets and our stereo (forgot brand)

CHARGE
A charge has been lasting a good six to eight hours for us. Recharging seems to take us about three hours.

THE BOTTOM LINE
These are comfortable headphones that are easy to use, stay in the ears well, and have good insulation from ambient noise in the room or surroundings. They have nice highs and lows but tend to drown out the mids. The controls are a bit more challenging to learn at first as compared to other Bluetooth head sets we have used.

MY RATING
FOUR AND A HALF STARS- not able to give that so I am doing four. It is more like four and a half. The sound could be a little more balanced, and the controls not quite so difficult, but this is still a great set of headphones and we like it a lot.
text_fidelity_b: 1MORE iBFree In-Ear Earphones Wireless Headphones with Bluetooth 4.2 AAC, IPX 6 Waterproof, Secure Fit, In-Line Mic for Sports Gym Running - New Model Black

No subscription needed (if you install a micro and card). They do offer a cloud storage option, which is nice, and they offer an option to insert a micro and card to store locally- which is exactly what I was looking for. I just popped out my card out of my Nintendo switch to test it out.

This little security camera began picking up motion and sound right away (fyi, you need to go into settings to switch on the alerts). So, yeah I’m glad I got this small (but mighty) little security camera! I’m thinking of buying one for my back porch now, to see how well it holds up outside!

Cons: App lags a little. Could just be my internet speed, but the live stream doesn’t start right away when I go to view. When this happens, I close out of the app and open it again and it’s all good. Not really enough for me to knock a star off for. But it’s something I’d like to note.

Only issue is the coil whine, which is a roll of the dice. Worst case scenario it'll whine all the time like the first one I tried, whereas my newest replacement only does it during memory tests - which is acceptable.

But other than that, it's excellent. The Carbon and Strix-E both had issues getting my 7200 kit stable at XMP, and I spent almost a week straight tweaking voltages on the Strix - it would always eventually error out in Karhu after 30-60 minutes or so. The Master however is rock solid, and I was able to OC to 7400cl34 with extreme stability. Its "Low Latency/High Bandwidth" options are excellent, and perform better than the XMP tweaked setting on the ASUS.

It also ran the 13900k the coolest, and seemed easier to get stable. Overall if you are lucky enough to not have one with coil whine, it's definitely the best option in this price range.

text_fidelity_a:
Regetek 7" Double DIN Touchscreen in Dash Bluetooth Car Stereo Mp3 Audio 1080P Video Player FM Radio/AM Radio/TF/USB/AUX-in + Remote Control I received this as a free review sample. The reason why I subtracted a star is the cables (both the one from the charger to the control module, and the 3.5mm connection) are hardwired. This means that if either cable becomes damaged it can cost more to repair than to replace, unless you have the skills to repair them. Had the charger been configured with a micro USB port and the control module with a 3.5mm port for separate cables that can be easily purchased just about anywhere (including pharmacies and supermarkets these days), a damaged cable would be an easy swap and the value and utility of this solution been a lot more.

Operationally, this kit functions as promised. The mic will pass through commands if your phone has voice recognition, and the overall quality of sound is more a function of your vehicle's stereo system than this unit. Since my vehicle is already bluetooth-enabled I used a small, powered speaker with a 3.5mm input to test this. Since the cable, as mentioned, is fixed I had to still perform the test in my vehicle. The sound quality was overall good, and making and receiving test calls were easy and the connections clear enough to be heard without 'can you hear me now?'

Surprisingly the extra USB port in the charger was relatively fast, and proved to be as good as any high-speed (but non QC) charger on both my Note 4 and a friend's iPhone 5S. In fact, that is why I only subtracted one star because while the cable issue does detract, the charging capability of the extra port is better than I expected.

Bottom line: this is an OK hand's free solution for older vehicles that have an AUX port, but no bluetooth (and you NEED an AUX port to make this work.) Since the control module is hardwired into a lighter-style charger you cannot use this with a home stereo that does not have bluetooth, but does have 3.5mm input. There are similar solutions that use basically the same design, but replaceable cables that do allow this, so this one is restricted to vehicle-only use. If that is all you need, this one does perform as claimed.
text_fidelity_b: Regetek 7" Double DIN Touchscreen in Dash Bluetooth Car Stereo Mp3 Audio 1080P Video Player FM Radio/AM Radio/TF/USB/AUX-in + Remote Control

text_fidelity_a:
IDEALROYAL Smart Watch, Fitness Tracker for Android Phones, Smartwatch with Heart Rate,Sleep Monitor,Activity Tracker with IP67 Waterproof Pedometer Watch for Android & iOS for Men Women At time of writing, this is going for $30, but I think it may have been $20 previously. I was surprised to see those prices, because it seems pretty sophisticated. I don't have an Apple watch, but I don't imagine it does much more than this (although I could definitely be wrong). It's a shame that wearing a watch sort of irritates me because I can see a real point to having this, surprisingly.

I think the Apple watch may have wireless charging, whereas this uses a magnetic cable with a USB port on one end. This can be just a little tricky to ensure it's charging while on its side (I guess face down is fine, but then you can't be 100% certain it's actually charging), but you get the hang of it quickly.

You get a surprising amount of information on the small face, and then a few scrolls in whichever direction can give you more information. You get use to that very quickly, too, and it is, in fact, very intuitive. You can always find what you want before too long.

The main face can be flash updated, meaning you can download different themes to the device. There's a couple neat ones, but nothing too exciting. I'm guessing there may be user uploaded versions for the Apple version (or maybe not, as Apple always locks its stuff down too much), and that could happen here, too, but I'm guessing not as many people have this, which will lessen the available "content".

The step count is the main thing, along with the time. The watch usually pops on for you to see it when you raise it to look at it, but not always. Usually a shake will turn it on if it doesn't notice you raise your arm. If nothing else, you can press the button. It's a fine line, because too many false positives would also be annoying.

It seems to last a very long time, like many days. And the battery indicator has five segments instead of the three that some devices have, so you get a better indication of when you'll have to charge it.

I'm not really convinced it's super accurate with my steps, but I'm not sure the Apple version would be either. And then it makes a guess on your calorie burn based on steps, which is just for fun as far as I'm concerned. It can do a bunch of other stuff if you hook it up with your "health" app, but I never bothered setting up that app in the first place.

Other convenience factors include it vibrating when you get a call or text, which can help you notice calls and texts, especially if you have your phone on vibrate all the time like I do (and for that reason miss a lot of calls). You can also read your text messages on here, although not really so well that you wouldn't just pull your phone out of your pocket if you actually want to read it (although knowing if you can ignore it can be helpful). You can also control your music to some degree and tell your camera to take a picture, which will be wonderful if you're one of those people always taking pictures of themselves (of if you just want a picture of you and your friends without having to have someone stay behind to press the button).

It also has a timer. Some of these things require the app to be running on your phone (I'm not saying which ones for sure because I think the manual said the camera shutter wouldn't work without the app, but it does). And there is a "find phone" feature which I can't figure out how to get to work, although I haven't tried much. I mean, it's bluetooth, so if the phone is far away, it won't help you anyway.

The watch and the band look just like the Apple version from what I can tell. The band also comes off easily, so I'm assuming it can be replaced with anything that fits the Apple version, but double-check before you count on it.

Overall, I like it a lot. I'd never consider the Apple version, which I assume costs hundreds, but for a fraction of that, I think it's a pretty cool toy.
text_fidelity_b: IDEALROYAL Smart Watch, Fitness Tracker for Android Phones, Smartwatch with Heart Rate,Sleep Monitor,Activity Tracker with IP67 Waterproof Pedometer Watch for Android & iOS for Men Women

iCrius Reading Light for Bed, Table Lamps for Bedroom, Dimmable LED Desk Lamp I received this as a free review sample. It is close to being perfect, but there is one thing that prevented me from awarding it five stars: the power cable is hardwired into the lamp. It's basically a standard USB cable that should have been a standard USB micro or USB C style, but is instead unremovable from the lamp. That means that if you damage the cable instead of replacing it with a readily available USB cable the repair cost is probably greater than replacing the entire lamp - unless you are handy at such things.

Aside from the cable, I love this lamp. For one thing the clamp will firmly hold the entire lamp in place on a music stand's thin, metal shelf. Plus the gooseneck, while flexible,holds the lamp where you place it. I have similar lamp that will move position if you bump it, so for me this one is vastly better than most.

I do love the fact that I can power this from a wall using the included charging adapter or from a battery such as a [[ASIN:B014O2AXB0 Kikicom Power Bank]] (or similar model). Also you can actually power it from a laptop's USB port, which makes it perfect for small study desks. The included charger has a 1 Amp port for powering the lamp and a port marked 2.1 Amps for charging phones and tablets. To be honest, the 2.1 port is not especially fast and I suspect outputs less than the labeled capacity, but it still can keep up with my tablet.

Bottom line: if you area musician this is possibly the best music stand lamp in its price range (and it is not described as a music stand lamp!) For reading and even small room lighting it is also excellent. It would be an easy five stars had the cable been standard.

text_fidelity_a:
Logitech Optical Trackball Marble Mouse Logitech Trackball Marble Mouse is one of the better computer accessories I have used and it offers a noticeable improvement compared to traditional computer mice. Its unique shape makes it much more comfortable and a no- sliding- necessary design eliminates the need to drag your mouse across a flat surface to move the computer pointer on your screen. To move the pointer, all you do is move the large, red marble trackball. There is less strain on the fingers and wrist, making for a more comfortable experience.

Besides the added comfort, another advantage of the Logitech Trackball Marble Mouse is that it requires less space than a traditional mouse. Because this mouse is stationary and doesn't need to be dragged across a desk or other surface, it can fit into many small spaces. You don't need to make room to drag it, so it can be placed in tight quarters. This is great for those who work in offices with limited desk space.

The Logitech Trackball Marble Mouse offers four buttons to use for clicking. The large tabs on each side of the mouse are used for the usual right and left click functions and then there are two smaller tabs right above each of the larger tabs that are used for various functions. These two small tabs can be programmed to perform several things, and many will likely program them to scroll since this Logitech mouse doesn't have a scroll wheel. But the tabs can be programmed for other things, too. Since I don't necessarily need to scroll, my small tabs have been programmed as browser back and forward buttons. This makes life a little easier because I no longer need to move my mouse to the top of my screen and click the forward and backward arrows in the upper left corner. I just click my small left tab to go back and my small right tab to go forward.

The Logitech Trackball Marble Mouse is a marked improvement compared to the standard mouse, but I admit that it does take some getting used to. Having used a traditional mouse for most of my computer- using years, I had grown accustomed to sliding my mouse across the desk surface. Thus, when I started to use the Logitech Trackball Marble Mouse, I kept sliding it around on my desk also, even though I knew this mouse didn't need to be dragged. It took some time to break this habit. It also took time to get used to the sensitivity of the trackball. The slightest movement sends your pointer flying and when I first started to use this mouse, I would continually underestimate the precision of the Logitech Trackball Marble Mouse. My movements of the trackball were far too extreme. The pointer would soar across my computer screen, even though I would swear I wasn't moving the trackball very much. It is a very sensitive device that almost seems too loose at first because it moves so freely and with such little effort.

Compared to a traditional mouse, the Logitech Trackball Marble Mouse has many great things to offer and it is a mouse I am happy I took the time to try. It is superior to the traditional model in most areas, reducing pain and strain and offering greater accuracy and an easy grip. It does take time to get used to, but it is worth it in the long run and even those who initially resist the change will be happy, in due time, that they made the switch to Logitech.
text_fidelity_b: Logitech Optical Trackball Marble Mouse

text_fidelity_a:
Echo Show 8 (1st Gen, 2019 release) -- HD smart display with Alexa – stay connected with video calling - Sandstone I purchased this for two reasons: a convenient way to display recipes that didn't require my phone being out, and streaming movies for when I'm in the kitchen for hours at a time.

I rely heavily on streaming during the holiday seasons while I bake to fulfill orders, and while the video quality was good, and the sound was AMAZING, the rest of the device was too troublesome to be worth it.
Example: Open amazon video, and it gives you 4 categories to go through, or your library. I go to my library (severe lag every single time) and I find the movie I want. I hit play, severe lag again, and it plays. Quality is not bad at all, especially for the price, but heaven forbid you have to pause. Once you pause for ~2-3 minutes, it goes to a screen saver. And when you unlock it, you have to go through the process of finding the movie all over again. It's a pain in the butt. They could at least have a "continue watching..." at the beginning of the prime menu, but it doesn't.

Secondly, our household has 3 users on our hulu account--if there was a way to switch users through the Echo, I didn't see it. I googled it, thinking I was overlooking it, and nothing. We all have very different tastes for shows/movies, and never use each others accounts for this reason. To have not one, but two streaming services being out of the question/too inconvenient to use, I couldn't handle it.

The integration was wonky at best. I have an echo dot that resides on a window sill about 3 feet from where I had my echo. My echo was off for voice recognition, but when I'd talk to my dot, it would display on my echo. This was cool except for two things: 1. It did it intermittently. 1 out of 3 times it would mirror to the echo. 2. if you were streaming something when the echo mirrored what the dot was telling you, guess what, YOU HAVE TO FIND THE MOVIE AGAIN. It was a nightmare.

Maybe down the road they'll figure out a more user friendly programming for this, but until then I'm returning it. It was meant to be a gift for family, but if I, an electronic savvy 30-something, can't figure it out, I wouldn't be comfortable giving it to my grandparents, which was the end goal.
text_fidelity_b: Echo Show 8 (1st Gen, 2019 release) -- HD smart display with Alexa – stay connected with video calling - Sandstone

text_fidelity_a:
Linksys AC1900 Wi-Fi Wireless Dual-Band+ Router with Gigabit & USB 3.0 Ports, Smart Wi-Fi App Enabled to Control Your Network from Anywhere (EA6900) When I first set up a home network, I selected a Cisco "Linkys" G router (EA1300) because I recognized the brand name. Later I upgraded to a Cisco dual-band N router ([[ASIN:B007IL7AKM Linksys EA4500]]), which was--and still is--a superb router. My latest upgrade, to this LINKSYS AC1900 (EA6900) DUAL BAND SMART WI-FI ROUTER, represents another leap forward in the performance of my home network.

The wireless signal is stronger in every corner of my two-story condo. All of my devices (some 25 computers, tablets, music players, Kindles, cellphones, Roku, etc.) connect very quickly. Best of all, I'm getting Comcast's promised high-speed Internet speeds of more than 50 Mbps with the Comcast-supplied new telephony modem. (An online speed test site just now clocked the download speed at 57 Mbps). In fact, my present home network is capable of even faster speeds--the home network is limited by the speed of the slower external Comcast network.

This router is extremely easy to set up. You just connect it, and follow the prompts from the built-in software. Whenever you access the router to adjust the settings, and click on some part of the Menu, you find excellent "contextual" help screens that fully explain the meaning of each of the settings. The Menu is set up differently from the menus for the EA4500 and EA1300, but the basic methodology for the settings is the same--the settings are just presented in a way that's easier for a non-techie user to understand.

I read a newspaper review that recommended NOT buying this excellent EA6900 router, because of testers' problems with the second band and with nonfunctioning USB ports. I think that the testers probably received a defective router--and should have requested a replacement. Even a reliable brand like Cisco may sometimes ship an occasional bad electronics device.

Because I only need a single-band router, I haven't tested the second band on my EA6900 router. (The second band did work fine on my EA4500 router, but using the second band didn't improve the signal strength, so I didn't continue using it.) However, I did test the USB ports on the EA6900, and both work really well. In fact, the router recognized and easily accessed a couple of external wireless storage drives--connected with a 100-foot (!) USB cable--when my PC was flakey about recognizing those same drives when they were connected directly to the PC with the long cable.

I absolutely love this EA6900 router, which I've been using for more than a month now. Because of my home wiring, the router is located a long way from any of my wireless devices, and I have a lot of nearby neighbors with competing wireless Internet connections. But with the EA6900, there have been virtually no dropped connections, and the strong signal is something that I've long been wishing for!
text_fidelity_b: Linksys AC1900 Wi-Fi Wireless Dual-Band+ Router with Gigabit & USB 3.0 Ports, Smart Wi-Fi App Enabled to Control Your Network from Anywhere (EA6900)

text_fidelity_a:
Cooler Master MasterBox Q300L Micro-ATX Tower & Thermaltake Toughpower GX2 80+ Gold 600W SLI/Crossfire Ready Continuous Power ATX 12V V2.4/EPS V2.92 Non Modular Power Supply Only two issues are that the stock fan that comes with the case is not quiet, and there is no area for a disk drive. Everything else about this case is pretty cool. Cable management was much easier than the other three cases I have worked with. HDD/SDD management is really neat--it's behind the motherboard instead of at the front base of the case, saving precious room for large GPUs if that is your thing. His computer is not RGB, but this thing would look darn cool with RGB.

I really like how the case is the size of a mATX case, but it can comfortably fit a standard ATX motherboard due to the ability to change where the PSU goes.

At this moment, I cannot speak for how cool the case keeps yet, but the whole thing is essentially a grate, so I can't imagine the air flow being bad. I suggested he get a few more fans just to keep air flowing through the filters, as they impede flow a fair amount, just like all the non-foam filters I've dealt with. If need be, the filters can be easily removed to allow the system to cool more effectively.

If I need to get a new case for some reason, I will probably get this.
text_fidelity_b: Cooler Master MasterBox Q300L Micro-ATX Tower & Thermaltake Toughpower GX2 80+ Gold 600W SLI/Crossfire Ready Continuous Power ATX 12V V2.4/EPS V2.92 Non Modular Power Supply

Kindle Voyage E-reader, 6" High-Resolution Display (300 ppi) with Adaptive Built-in Light, PagePress Sensors, Wi-Fi It's just plain spectacular how good the Kindle Voyage is.

I'm kind of a gadget junkie. Whenever a new Kindle reader comes out, I pass on the old one and buy the new. So I'm coming from a place that has used everything from the old Kindle Keyboard through to this, my newest Kindle, the Kindle Voyage 3G.

First, screen quality. I knew it had 300 v. 221 PPI I had on my PW2, but until I saw it, couldn't believe how much of a difference it made. Now, the PW2 screen is great, but this beats it soundly. For regular reading, I don't see any reason to switch from a PW2 to a Voyage, but I'd imagine that with illustrations and such, it would make a really big difference. I can actually read at one size smaller font than I could on the PW2.

The light: Nice light, no weird shadings. My device is smoothly lit from bottom to top.

Size/Weight: It's smaller, definitely (not the screen though). Couldn't really see any difference in weight between this and the PW2, but honestly, what's an ounce either way, especially once you start sticking covers on it? It's not something I particularly care about.

Storage/Memory: I wish it were a bit bigger. Not that I have any desire to have 2,000 on my Kindle at any given time, but once you get into using about half the memory, these devices always slow down and get ornery.

Wishes/Dreams for the next e-reader: That they'd include text to voice. I doubt this will happen, but I wish it would.

text_fidelity_a:
AKASO Brave 4 4K 20MP WiFi Action Camera Ultra HD with EIS 30m Waterproof Camera Remote Control 5X Zoom Underwater Camcorder with 2 Batteries and Helmet Accessories Kit Support External Microphone Akaso Brave 4 (Updated) Review

Note: WiFi apps tested using a Google LG Nexus 5x without a sim card, which is a spare phone I use to control my GoPro Hero4. I haven't tested it with my Galaxy S9, because I don't plan to use them together. You may have different results with a different phone, and there may be a better app than the recommended one. LD Cam, for instance, almost works better, but not quite.

Note2: Manufacturer claims "Since 4K resolution is too big, APP does not support." Well, the GoPro app does. I think it's the software library used in many of the other apps that limit the size to 1080p. USB transfers work extremely well. It identifies as a USB drive on the PC and other devices.

Pros:
-Inexpensive compared to GoPro (less than a used Hero 4 Black)
-4K/24fps is higher frame rate than GoPro Hero 4
-Simple to use (other than the WiFi app)
-Plenty of useful settings and features
-Can be used with a PC as a webcam
-Windows 10 recognizes it and loads a driver for it
-Connects via USB-OTG to Galaxy S9 flawlessly for transferring files
-Doesn't overheat like both my GoPro Hero 4 and Hero 7 Black.
-Very lightweight.
-Works great when set up as a dash cam.
-Doesn't overheat and shut down like a GoPro.

Cons:
-Recommended WiFi apps don't support 4K (yet?)
-Recommended WiFi apps require mobile data be turned off (even without a sim card)
-Recommended WiFi apps don't stay connected with my Nexus 5x
-WiFi apps reset camera settings to arbitrary values
-WiFi has to be turned off and back on and app restarted if it disconnects
-Battery cover could be easier to remove
-Not a rugged camera (though not that heat sensitive)
-Klemme 1, an open tripod mount, doesn't hold the camera firmly so wouldn't work as an action mount (used a heat gun to tighten it up and it's tolerable now.

Other:
Though this looks like a GoPro Hero 4, and is very similar in size and layout, it's only similar. They're different enough to prevent using a Hero 4 case. Not much. Just a little. But enough. That's unfortunate, because the Suptig case I have works with an external battery that allows me to record for several hours (5+) with the Hero 4. I was hoping this would work with that case, but it won't. That's what happens when I have unreasonable expectations.

It abruptly adjusts to changing light conditions but lags slightly behind during rapidly changing conditions, particularly when using time-lapse, so that going from the darkness under a bridge to bright sunlight while driving often results in a total whiteout. I haven't notice the same effect with the GoPro Hero 4, and I suspect that it ramps a bit more slowly from darkness to light to avoid this effect.

If the recommended WiFi app, or the alternative worked better, I'd give it one more star (gave it that one more star after using it as a dash cam). Even with all the cons relating to WiFi, I actually like the camera, and think it's worth the ~$80 I paid for it.
text_fidelity_b: AKASO Brave 4 4K 20MP WiFi Action Camera Ultra HD with EIS 30m Waterproof Camera Remote Control 5X Zoom Underwater Camcorder with 2 Batteries and Helmet Accessories Kit Support External Microphone

text_fidelity_a:
PHILIPS 3 Ft. USB Type C Cable, USB-A to USB-C Red Durable Braided Fast Charging Cable, Compatible with iPad Pro, MacBook Pro, Samsung Galaxy S21/S10/S9/Plus, Google Pixel 5/C/3/2/XL, DLC5203RA/37 Thank you in advance to the Amazon VINE program for providing an item to review. A positive review was not required, nor was it requested, and all words are my own.

One thing I sadly use a lot of – phone/USB cables for charging and data transfer. These are almost as bad as the AUX cables for my car and iPod.

So, seeing this was a Philips one – I honestly thought I lucked out. I was going to give my old cable to my mom as hers was cracking near the "C" port. I figured I could use this one - she could have my old one.

It is a DURABLE cable and looked like it would go through quite a bit. The length is perfect for charging with an adapter connected to a power strip on the floor. And, it can also plug into the USB ports on a computer (or so equipped power strip).

So, why a one star rating?

This does not work. I tried with my phone and my mom’s phone. NADA. Nothing. I tried connecting it to the adapter – nothing. Tried using just the USB cable to a USB port on a power strip (which was on since it is powering my computer) – NOTHING.

So, I tried using a USB port on my computer. NOTHING. Tried with a “USB hub” connected to my computer. There was a slight problem. The “buttons” on the port light up when a port is turned on. Despite the port for this cord being on – the lights didn’t light up. Other items connected – my external mouse and a USB flash drive – they were turned off when this cord was connected.

Needless to say – this is BELOW one star. It doesn’t even work. But, I do have to rate it something.

I could’ve gotten a bad cable – after all, there is no damage to it or the packaging. But, it still doesn't work. But, I can’t return it since it was free.
text_fidelity_b: PHILIPS 3 Ft. USB Type C Cable, USB-A to USB-C Red Durable Braided Fast Charging Cable, Compatible with iPad Pro, MacBook Pro, Samsung Galaxy S21/S10/S9/Plus, Google Pixel 5/C/3/2/XL, DLC5203RA/37

text_fidelity_a:
MEE audio M6 X1 Wired In-Ear Sports Headphones with Microphone and Remote – Sweatproof Secure Fit Earphones for Running, Jogging, and Gym Workouts (Black) (EP-X1-GYBK) Even pre break-in, these sounded great: probably the best headphones under $20 I've found. After break-in, these MEE buds were sounding like something that cost 4-5 times as much with a nice, even frequency response that favors bass only slightly. I find them comparable to $60-$80 Sennheisers, my previous favorites (which superseded Sony and Koss buds that I also liked). These MEE buds came with 3 sets (S, M, and L) of your typical soft rubber earpieces as well as 2 sets of the interesting multi-tiered earpieces shown in the photos and a pretty standard cloth case. Between the various earpiece options, it's unlikely anyone will have an issue finding a good fit.

The cord is about 1 m long, which suits my purposes. I like the over-the-ear wire bits, too, as they prevent tugs on the cord from dislodging them. They might be awkward with some kinds of glasses, but my straight-earpiece sunglasses fit over them fine. They can be bent to hang down more like normal earbuds if desired, though.

I'll be checking out more MEE products now, seeing what a great value these were. I still favor AKG and Beyerdynamic at the high end, but for my biking/hiking/running/workout listening needs, I'll probably be coming back to MEE.
text_fidelity_b: MEE audio M6 X1 Wired In-Ear Sports Headphones with Microphone and Remote – Sweatproof Secure Fit Earphones for Running, Jogging, and Gym Workouts (Black) (EP-X1-GYBK)

Most of mine are in the price range $20-30, so those are the ones I'm using for comparison. Based on that, these new Pioneer earbuds seem to be the best of that group.

I listen mostly to classical music with a smattering of other genres (folk, 1960s-70s rock, Broadway). These provided acceptable performance for all genres, but do seem to lack some low-end bass response. One of my test recordings is the Erich Kunzel/Cincinnati Symphony recording of Tchaikovsky's "1812 Overture" with cannons, and the low-end loss was noticeable. Still, the rest of the sound is excellent, and these will work just fine for my day-to-day listening -- music that I have going on in the background while working on something else. For serious listening, I'll use my over-the-ear headphones.

Good performance for the price. I like these.

Having this EZVIZ video camera, it can't get any easier.

Have been using a different video device for the past year. So wanted to see how this one compared.
Very easy set up. Using the quick set up guide, can have this up and running within a few minutes including downloading the needed app.
Long power cord with this. Can easily plug it in and have enough cord for it to reach a much higher level. Right now I have mine on a small shelf on the wall. If I choose to run it to the ceiling, (sticky pad included to do this) I will definitely get a nice cord cover to hide the cord that would be hanging down the wall to the outlet.
I like that it has audio so I'm able to talk and listen to whoever is in the room. Has nice night vision and was able to see the room when I only had a small night light on.
Video quality is really nice and clear. And love the wide angle with this. I can actually see the entire room.
Because I have animals, I have decided not to activate the motion detection. I really don't need alerts, to my phone, every time a dog moves around.
It's nice that I can buy a larger SD memory card for this. I will probably just increase it to 64GB. I really don't want to pay for cloud service so opted out of buying that.
No updates yet so not sure how well the "one-click updates" will work. But, if it works, it will be fantastic adding new features and functionality with just one click.
This is my first EZVIZ security camera but will love letting me see all of my EZVIZ cameras in one place if I choose to buy some more.

Great video security camera, for a decent price, that will definitely get used a LOT.
Would love to expand and eventually have my whole house monitored.

I synced this with iPad, iPhone and iPod Classic (using Kokkia I10). The quality of the sound is fabulous as you would expect from BOSE ( a lot of bass) you will not be disappointed. The range is not miles...more like 20 feet..and not through too many walls. ...terrific design of compactness and total comfort on my ears. In terms of external noise, it really did cut out the concrete jungle living of traffic hum.

I listened to my music for over an hour now and no pain on my ears...bliss and worth every cent and pennies. I love these new BOSE Bluetooth headphones. Note, they come fully charged. The headphones remember all the names of the gadgets, and will play from which ever one that is 'on', which is a huge plus. There appears to be an intelligence here that we do not see in the Bose over the ear wireless headphones.

text_fidelity_a:
JLab Rewind Wireless Retro Headphones | Bluetooth 4.2 | 12 Hours Playtime | Custom EQ3 Sound | Music Controls | Noise Isolation | with Microphone | Throwback 80s 90s Design | Black I wasn't expecting much given the price of this item, and I got pretty much what I expected.

The charging port is hard to reach and the LED charging indicator is difficult, if not impossible to see, without having to move the foam earpiece covering.

Setting up/pairing the device is pretty easy. Press the button for 4 seconds or so and you’ll hear a pleasant female voice say, “Hello”. This means the power is on. Continue holding the button and the device will enter pairing mode. You’ll hear the voice say, “Ready to pair.” When pairing is complete, you’ll hear the device say, “You’re connected” and tell you how much charge the battery has. So far, all I’ve heard is, “Battery full.” I have no idea what other battery indications the voice will give – perhaps only at 3/4, 1/2 and 1/4? Or maybe percentages?

The buttons are the biggest drawback with this device. Actually, it's really just one multi-function button on the right earpiece. The button functionality is not like any Bluetooth headset I've used before - very non-intuitive. The button has no label at all and the tactile feedback is nonexistent at times - I press the button sometimes and there's no "click" feeling. If a song is playing, it doesn't seem to matter where I press, the song stops if it is playing. When I press again, anywhere, it starts playing again.

There is no volume control on the headphones at all. You’ll have to adjust the volume from your phone/audio player. There is a bare bones EQ function. You control this by clicking the multi-function button 3 times in rapid succession. Each time you do this, the device advances to the next of 3 EQ setting – balanced, bass boost and JLab signature. The “balanced” setting seems to sound just like what it’s named – balanced or equal high, mid and low tones. The bass boos is decent – not overbearing. Not sure what the last one is, but if the pictograms in the manual are any indication, it boost the high and low ends. The EQ function does provide audible feedback – the voice announces each setting by name.

There's a next track function, but no function for going to the previous track. The next track function requires holding down the multi-function button for 2 seconds. There's no audible feedback for this function (other than a very short moment of silence). When you hear the silence, let go IMMEDIATELY. If you hold the button down for too long the Bluetooth connection will be severed and you'll have to reconnect.

Apparently, there's no ability to fast forward or rewind within a song or audio book. You'll have to do this on your phone/audio player. Pretty poor design if you ask me. BTW – I use this only with my audio player, so I did not test the phone/mic functions, but I’d be surprised if they were robust.

The instructions are minimal at best. The manual is one piece of paper printed on 2 sides. Unfolded, it's about the size of 2 business cards - about 4"x4.5" (10.16cm x 11.43cm). One side has instructions and the other is all promotions/disclaimers, etc. That's it.

Sound quality is acceptable - decent bass and stereo separation is good. I’m no audiophile though. The product description says it has "Noise Isolation", which is marketing speak used by all on-ear headphone manufacturers. It simply means the ambient noise is slightly reduced because the headphones cover your ears. Bottom line - there's no tech/function in this device that does any active noise cancellation.

The headphones are a little snug/tight, but not so much to be uncomfortable - at least that's my opinion after an hour+ of testing. Not sure if this will be true for something like a 3-4 hour flight. I’ll test this out in the near future and will update this review, if possible.

The charging cable that comes with the item is 9” long (22.86cm). Not very useful at all, but better than nothing.

On the plus side, the manufacturer did provide an extra set of foam earpiece covers - the set that comes on the headphones is orange. The extra set is black.

Bottom line, for $15 I wasn't expecting a lot - well maybe better button functionality, but hey, what can you do? As my granddad used to say, “You pays your money and you takes your chances.”
text_fidelity_b: JLab Rewind Wireless Retro Headphones | Bluetooth 4.2 | 12 Hours Playtime | Custom EQ3 Sound | Music Controls | Noise Isolation | with Microphone | Throwback 80s 90s Design | Black

Projector with WiFi and Bluetooth, VIMGO Native 1080P Portable Projector 4K Supported 120" Display for Home Outdoor, Dustproof Smart Mini Projector, Zoom 50%, Compatible with iOS/Android/PS5/TV Stick I must confess and give a shout out- I follow the “phantom of Amazon” as he’s practically reviewed every home projector Ive looked at.. Following his detailed pro/cons lists and why- helped make my decision. He’s a person in the business and knows his stuff.. So, when HE named this one/if not the best in tower projectors (in this price point) I took his advice and I’m thrilled I did!!

As one with zero tech skills- I needed that “guru advice” on a subject I didn’t understand. Along with a few “how to” videos for confidence (I suggest doing this prior to use if unsure on using- it lends so much in the way of confidence!) Im thrilled that one’s advice sent me to the “tower style..” If I set on nightstand or TV tray- it’s truly a perfect height for the screen or mid section of a wall to give you an idea.

What I found myself: Its vital to get projector with auto focus BUT, also have ability to fine tune the focus by hand- it gets your picture SO crystal clear. And bc furniture is on carpet- a stabilizer lets you even it up (we had x1 side off from edge of screen every time.. ugh!) We havent used outside yet- but on grass etc.. a stabilizer will be a necessity!!

Hack 1: Read instructions- SAVE THEM SAFELY IN PLASTIC SLEEVE/BAG! double side tape sleeve inside box or projector case (must buy separately!) keeps info. safe and easy to locate always! Hack 1A: using an insulated lunch pack can double as carry case and may even save you $. Hack 2: depending on where using.. who knows how close to power source you’ll be. *Keep extension cord w/ projector. Doing so will avoid disappointment or obstacle as one goes to use!!

Blue tooth is the bomb!! If turned on- it will try to auto sync by sending an invitation to device.. if you follow the prompts, it holds your hand thru all the steps to connect! Funny to see ME type all this..but, trust me- if I can navigate process you can x1000!!! Note: we didn’t need an extra speaker.. x5 of us could hear just fine from the projector alone.. sound is heard on all sides- NICE!! *My son played PS4 games using projector and I actually had to tell him to turn down volume!! Projector was causing too much ruckus- ha.. that’s always a good sign!

So grateful this is user-friendly and end results surpassed all expectations. I so recommend getting a specified bag/backpack to transport and store the projector in.. it protects your investment and keeps it contained! Hoping info can help decision making in a layman sort of way! sorry so long-winded.. stay safe everyone.

TP-Link N300 Wireless Portable Nano Travel Router(TL-WR802N) - WiFi Bridge/Range Extender/Access Point/Client Modes, Mobile in Pocket I purchased this to try and create my own wireless network within a hospital room I would be in for a while. The problem as many have stated is most commercial WiFi system require you log into a splash page after you connect to their network. This router does not have a way to do that. You can try using one of your devices and then clone the MAC address to the router, but this only works if this router is connected to the network with the Ethernet cable port. Most hotels and hospitals no longer have working Ethernet jacks in rooms. If you try and clone the MAC address on the wireless port it creates a conflict and everything stops working.

So to sum up, it works fine as a cheap travel router, but if you have to deal with a splash page on an WiFi only network, it simply will not work. It can’t be that hard to create one of these with a built in browser for splash pages. Anyone listening????

text_fidelity_a:
FULLJA WiFi Digital Picture Frame - 10.1 Inch Smart Digital Photo Frame with FHD IPS Touch Screen, 32GB Memory, Motion Sensor WiFi Electronic Picture Frame Share Photos and Videos Via App Email I don’t love it. This seems overpriced for what you get. For the price, I was expecting it to look more like a photo frame but instead, it kinda feels like an old monitor. My goal was to hang it on the wall during art shows with process videos playing. It will work OK for that but I’m disappointed that unless the video is in the exact proportion of the frame, it will always look a little “off” and there’s no means of changing how it’s framed in the display.

I think it’s at its best without the clock or any other additions.

The pros: It really does work right out of the box. It only took minutes to get photos onto it. The big screen is nice, I can see details in my photos. It is also bright with vivid colors. I like that it is flat which is why it performs better than an average monitor as a picture frame. The simple black frame doesn’t detract from its appearance. I like that there is an app and my husband and I were able to add photos, and I also like that there is a way to add photos via card in case software changes make the app obsolete. With the app, I was able to get videos onto it in minutes. I also like that it has a large amount of storage space and the means to expand it..

The cons: It is slow. I didn’t love the way the photos are displayed. I also hate the default animations because they are a bit cheesy. I want it to fade or some other non-intrusive way to change photos, and there is no means to edit it. The features are incredibly barebones. I hate that the default includes the time etc, I just want it to look like a photo frame! The audio is a bit tinny, much more so than a television etc. I also find it bizarre in 2023 to have an item that warns that it can destroy a USB if it’s removed without turning it off first…that seems like such an old-school problem!

I wish the plug was white because the black looks bad against the wall, and I prefer a minimalist look.

For the price, I feel like this could be better. There are just so few options for customizing the display.

The system that allows remote viewing is unable to reboot itself when power is restored, so if your home loses power for some reason while you are not home, the sync Module does not automatically reconnect when the power comes back on. This ultimately renders the whole system useless since it can’t be relied upon when you are not home.

My original system, Zmodo does air reconnect so if my home loses power, the cameras reconnect as soon as they have power again. In fact the cameras were what alerted us to the return of power to our home during the 2016 fires in Napa. I will stick with them, despite the wiring issue. They are just more reliable.

kopack Deluxe Black Laptop Backpack, 17 Inch Anti-Theft Water Resistant Laptop Backpack with Multiple Compartments for Business College Travel Commute Work Computer Daypack Men/Women They really designed this pack thoughtfully with a lot of consideration for style, utility, quality of materials, and the user's comfort. Constructed of water repellant nylon inside and out, this bag is impeccably stitched, has sturdy zippers that work flawlessly, a comfortable carry handle, and offers plenty of storage. In fact, the pack can hold two laptops up to 17" at the same time along with other gear.

Here's the layout:

Front - a 10" x 9" side opening zippered compartment, a 12" x 16" zippered compartment with 2 sleeves for cell phone, battery bank etc, 2 pen holding sleeves, plus a 10" x 4" zippered mesh compartment.

Sides - 4.5" x 7" beverage holders on each side that are large enough to accommodate even larger bottles and sit flush when not being used.

Main Compartment - double zipper provides entry and can be locked to prevent theft. Inside are two cell phone/gadget pouches, an 8" x 6" zippered compartment, and a 12" x 11" laptop or tablet sleeve with no padding on the front. I was able to fit my 15" Lenovo ThinkPad into this sleeve with room to spare and although the sleeve front isn't padded, the entire compartment t is surrounded with excellent padding. Plenty of room in the main compartment for a laptop or tablet, gear, folders, and some travel clothing or text books.

Rear - comfortable padded carry handle, the back unzips to reveal a large well padded compartment that can fit up to a 17" laptop. The back of the pack is thickly cushioned and also has thick mesh lined scapular and lumbar pads. Directly beneath the lumbar padding is a 11" x 6" zippered compartment that would be an excellent place to secure passports, travel documents, emergency cash, or other valuables.

Straps - thickly padded, mesh lined, and ergonomically curved, with a sunglasses loop on one side. The adjustment hardware is heavy duty plastic that functions smoothly and all of the stress points are well reinforced.

This is a very well designed laptop bag made of excellent materials that should be durable. It would function well for school, business, or travel, and it seems very reasonably priced considering the quality.

This backpack was provided at no cost for evaluation purposes.

text_fidelity_a: Amazon Smart Plug, for home automation, Works with Alexa - A Certified for Humans Device We bought this plug when it was on a deal for $5. Glad we only paid that for it because the plug finally stopped reconnecting to the internet this week. Previously if the power failed it would reconnect on it's own. Occasionally it would just drop from the internet at random and then I could easily connect it. Most of the time, however, it would work great! We use it for a light since most of our house works on light switches that are not conveniently placed near the doors, so we trip around at night over stuff to get to the actual lights to turn them on without the smart plugs. Well after a storm and a power surge this past week, the plug in our bedroom showed as disconnected in the app. I have tried multiple times over multiple days to reconnect it. Once it gets to the internet connection part of the pairing "Provisioning Failure" pops up and it won't connect at all. I contacted Amazon via chat to fix the issue (after troubleshooting myself) and they only suggested resetting the plug (which I had already done) and restarting our entire home system and each Amazon Smart Device (which we did after the power surge due to other devices not working). After an hour and a half, they basically said well its out of warranty so you need to buy a new one. They did offer a discount but the discount was to be issued as a refund after purchase and the amount to be paid was significantly more then what I originally paid. We have 2 other smart plugs of a different brand that are as old as this plug that have had absolutely no issues to date and cost about $5 each when we purchased them as well. Not to mention the Amazon Smart Plug is bulky and takes up so much more space then the smaller round off-brand ones. Due to the fact that this plug didn't last a long time and the actual price is so high to begin with I would not recommend this plug. Spend the money on an off-brand!
text_fidelity_b: Amazon Smart Plug, for home automation, Works with Alexa - A Certified for Humans Device

Logitech NEW Logitech Webcam C210 (Cameras & Frames) I received the Logitech VideoCam and was surprised at one, how easy and quick the setup took; second, I was amazed at the quality of the picture. This is my first time at WebCam and was apprehensive at the standard of quality. But in 1,2,3 steps it was up. The voices are clear and it depends whether you use Logitech viewing or Skype, but Logitech has a more refined lip movement to voice coordination. Again...this is a perfect picture!

Surprisingly, the 3MP photo option is quite impressive. I love the shoot picture instantly. You can quickly add a friend to chat with, just enter their email address. Either at your end of the recipients end you can quickly snap a picture and that pic can be the photo of choice for the friend or family. It is easy to have several different pictures on the interface of the Webcam; I dragged a few from the desktop. My webcam sits comfortably on top of the computer. If I need to remove the camera from the top of computer to show a different view of my background, or reveal other parts of the house, I can do that easily with the 5-feet long attached cord, although it could be longer.

You can make several adjustments, and the light adjustment is automatic, the mic is noise cancelling, however, I have not the need to test that yet.

What I like is that anytime someone on your contact list is at the computer, you can have a small message pop up that lets you know they are available. My two current contacts are using Windows XP; while I am on Windows Vista.

If you are someone you know is vascillating between getting a Webcam, I encourage them to do so, especially if they have family miles away like I do. Many people do not like to be on camera, and for me, I don't either because I have to look decent an any moment a call comes in. Try it.... You may like it! ....Rizzo

text_fidelity_a:
Logitech M570 Wireless Trackball Mouse – Ergonomic Design with Sculpted Right-Hand Shape, Compatible with Apple Mac / Microsoft, USB Unifying Receiver, Dark Gray (Discontinued by Manufacturer) I prefer trackballs to mice and I have been looking for a good wireless trackball as my primary system is a laptop. In the past I had a Logitech TrackMan II, a hideous device that made my hands hurt. Logitech's new M570 trackball is far and away better than that TrackMan II, and I would consider it an excellent device except for one thing.

I have large hands, and as a consequence I need larger pointing devices to fit my hand. The M570 is marginally larger than my standard mouse which gave me pause right off the bat, but my concerns were unfounded. Even though this trackball device is not especially large, it fits my hand comfortably and I can spin the ball with ease without cramping my hands. My finger tips rest on the buttons and my thumb tip rests on the ball, while the fleshy part of my palm is on the desk past the plastic base. Finally, a trackball that fits my hand much like a normal mouse.

I have a marble mouse and while it's a decent trackball-like device, the ball easily drops out when the device is inverted and as a result I have dropped the ball one too many times and chipped it. The M570 holds the ball in place and does not allow it to simply come out without applying deliberate pressure, resulting in less opportunities to either lose or damage the ball.

The ball itself is a pretty shade of blue and, with the exception of the finger holes, looks a lot like a miniature bowling ball.

The M570 has 4 buttons and a scroll wheel that can be pressed for a total of 5 programmable buttons. The one problem with this trackball involves the scroll wheel - there is no horizontal scroll. While this is really just an inconvenience, horizontal scrolling has become very commonplace and that it is not included is a disappointment.

The range on the M570 us excellent. I am able to control the pointer on the screen from a distance of 15' - 20' away without any issues at all (except that it's harder to read the screen). This is very convenient and will be immeasurably helpful for presentations where the desk is a good distance from the computer and control is needed across that distance.

I am very pleased with the Logitech M570 wireless trackball and can heartily recommend it. The one improvement would be horizontal scrolling; otherwise, this trackball is superb.
text_fidelity_b: Logitech M570 Wireless Trackball Mouse – Ergonomic Design with Sculpted Right-Hand Shape, Compatible with Apple Mac / Microsoft, USB Unifying Receiver, Dark Gray (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

I can only speak from my own experience and knowledge.

Amazon Basics Wireless Keyboard with Touchpad for Smart TV - US Layout (QWERTY) This AMAZON BASICS WIRELESS KEYBOARD (with Touchpad for Smart TV - US Layout (QWERTY)) has the easiest setup I’ve ever encountered for a wireless device. You insert 2 AAA batteries (included) into the keyboard, plug the USB radio receiver into a USB port on your Smart TV, and you’re instantly connected. If for some reason you aren’t automatically connected, you just hit Esc-K to connect.

The keyboard works with my Samsung QLED Q7F Smart TV. Not all of the function keys work with every screen--for example, the keyboard’s “Mute” button does NOT mute the TV--but that’s normal for generic controllers like this one that are intended to work with many different wireless devices.

The keyboard does everything that my Samsung remote does (for example, switches between apps, sources, calls up the TV settings menu), although it takes a bit of experimentation to learn how to use it. The direction keys near the touchscreen allow you to navigate the TV screen and everything else. If you go to the TV’s Internet area, the touchscreen activates and you see a big arrow cursor that works like a mouse.

The keyboard does the one thing that I really wanted. It has a Search button that allows me to search for TV shows, movies, etc. by typing on the keyboard, instead of by navigating around letter-by-letter on an onscreen letterpad. The keyboard does NOT work when I’m using Roku for searches, but that’s normal because the keyboard is designed to connect directly to a Smart TV (not to the TV’s connected accessories).

The keyboard does feel cheap, and I wouldn't want to use it as a computer keyboard. However, it's fine for my occasional use as a Smart TV keyboard.

NOTE: The wireless adapter is stored at the upper left of the box, inside the folded cardboard. The batteries are on the right.
text_fidelity_b: Amazon Basics Wireless Keyboard with Touchpad for Smart TV - US Layout (QWERTY)

text_fidelity_a:
Canon Powershot A1200 12.1 MP Digital Camera with 4x Optical Zoom (Silver) (OLD MODEL) OK, here are the facts: my other (similar) camera developed a glitch -- it will not allow me to delete photos without loooooong delays. So I went in search of an inexpensive replacement camera. I settled on this Canon.

I did so with trepidation because some of the reviews were lukewarm at best. Yet other reviewers loved it. (This, by the way, is what makes horse races!) So I thought I would take a chance.

Here is why I am happy with my choice: (1) the viewer seems larger than its dimensions suggest; (2) the camera fits in my shirt pocket; (3) the pics are crisp indoors and out; (4) the on-off button is clearly marked and the shot button is nice and robust. For me, these features are all I need. To be sure, the camera has a few video bells and whistles -- I'll try those one of these days. No rush.

A Con: the shot button takes a little getting used to, since it appears to have two stages to it. If you just press and disengage, nothing will happen. It requires a little patience and then it will take the picture. I can live with that idiosyncrasy.

Another Con: no internal memory. You must purchase an SD card before you can use the camera. This too I have accepted, because having pics on cards does make it easy to load them into PCs and laptops.

If you are looking for a simple "point-and-shoot" camera that will also perform other tricks if you are of a mind, go for it!
text_fidelity_b: Canon Powershot A1200 12.1 MP Digital Camera with 4x Optical Zoom (Silver) (OLD MODEL)

text_fidelity_a: Bose SoundLink Color Bluetooth Speaker (Blue) The only downsides to this product are that it doesn't charge while being plugged into an outlet and playing music simultaneously (major), the bass is in the back (very minor), and it takes a long time to charge (major). Outside of that, I'd buy these all day long. As long as you have line of sight, the bluetooth works over a very long distance! The bluetooth also works around corners and walls in medium distances. Yes, you get the crystal clear BOSE sound, and it is compact and works flawlessly. The connector is old school usb pin, similar to the older flip phones. It is loud, I wish it was louder outside. I also like the fact that multiple systems can connect to it at the same time. Great product, very convenient, and I've used this for tailgating, outdoor fire pit parties, and with my Mac and i-Phone. It works great!
text_fidelity_b: Bose SoundLink Color Bluetooth Speaker (Blue)
